task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-10-06, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: defensive suppression of opponent H2-H1 change
half-time adjustment (H2-H1) as a team-level outcome
methodological_questions: Is the defense effect on opponents' H2-H1 change stable across games, halves of a season, or seasons (split-half or year-to-year reliability)?
Does the 120 team-season sample have enough power to estimate a reliable defensive trait for H2-H1 change?
How much of the H2-H1 variance is noise, opponent quality, pace, and score-state or garbage-time effects rather than a team trait?
Which risks (regression to the mean, derived labels, leakage, base rate) threaten a test of this question?
evidence_establishes: Retrieval returned no records, so no earlier study by this project on this question or on related defensive H2-H1 reliability is available in this setting.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether defensive effects on opponents' H2-H1 change are reliable, stable, or absent.
Whether any earlier approach to this question failed, and for what reason.
Any effect size, reliability coefficient, or power figure for this metric.
own_inferences: Half-game scoring differences are noisy. With roughly 82 games per team-season, the standard error of a team's opponent-H2-H1 average is likely large relative to plausible between-team true variance, so reliability is probably low. This is an estimate from general basketball scoring variance, not from a record.

The 120 team-seasons are probably 30 teams across four regular seasons. A team-season-level correlation test would have modest power, and year-to-year stability can only be checked on about 90 consecutive-season pairs.
The 2025-26 season is complete for the regular season, so it can be used. The 2025-26 playoffs were partial before 2026-06-21 and must not be used before that date.
The question is probably answerable as a reliability question: if the reliability estimate is near zero, that is itself an informative answer.
uncertainties: The exact definition of 'defense effect' (regression coefficient, opponent-adjusted residual, or raw allowed differential) is not specified.
Whether playoff games are included in the 120 units is not stated; the regular season alone is assumed for the primary analysis.
Roster and coaching changes across the four seasons could break stability over time.
No historical records were returned, so the expected effect size and reliability are unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: No records were returned, so no earlier result changed the decision. The decision rests on the task statement and on the data description alone, and it is conditional on the reliability gate described in the design.

blocking_constraints.text: The H2-H1 change per team-season is probably dominated by game-level noise, so a defensive trait may not be recoverable without a reliability check first.
With 120 team-seasons, the year-to-year and split-half tests have limited power to detect a modest between-team true variance.
Opponent quality, pace, and score-state or garbage-time effects can produce H2-H1 differences that look like defensive suppression.

prior_work.summary: No prior work was retrieved, so it is unknown whether this question has been answered. No identifiers are cited.

risks.text: Per-team H2-H1 differences are noisy; split-half or season-to-season reliability may be too low to support a trait claim.
120 team-seasons give limited power for stability tests, especially after controlling for opponent and score state.
Selecting the best or worst defenses from one season and then testing them in the next season will overstate persistence through regression to the mean.
If the defense metric is built from the same H2-H1 points used as the outcome, the reliability estimate will be inflated.
Opponent quality, pace, home/away, and score-state or garbage-time effects can drive apparent defensive suppression of H2-H1 change.
Using 2025-26 playoff data before its completion date of 2026-06-21, or using full-season information to rate defenses before the games being predicted, would leak future information.
Testing several defensive metrics, halves, or splits will raise the chance of a spurious reliable-trait finding unless corrected.
Roster, coaching, and rule changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 can make defensive effects non-stationary, which lowers apparent year-to-year reliability.
Most teams probably have a near-zero true defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 change, so a supported result would be rare and easy to overstate.

design.estimand: Between-team true variance and reliability of the defense effect on opponents' H2-H1 scoring change, estimated with a mixed model that includes random team and opponent effects.
design.unit: Game-level opponent H2-H1 change nested in team-season; the team-season is the analysis unit for stability checks.
design.sample: Primary: NBA regular seasons 2022-23 to 2025-26 (120 team-seasons, regular season only). 2025-26 playoffs are excluded from the primary analysis and used only as a secondary check after 2026-06-21. No data after the analysis date is used.
design.power: Before analysis, estimate the minimum detectable reliability from the 120 team-seasons (target: ICC or split-half r at least 0.3 with a CI that excludes 0). If the CI is too wide to exclude a meaningful reliability, report inconclusive and do not claim a trait.
design.controls: Adjust for opponent strength (prior-season net rating), pace, home/away, and score margin at each half (garbage-time filter, e.g. exclude possessions with margin over 20). Use defensive matchup minutes to check that the metric does not simply reflect rotation or lineup mix. Derive the H1 and H2 splits from play-by-play only, not from a metric built on the same H2-H1 points.
design.falsification: Pre-register a null: split-half reliability of the defense effect within each season, and year-to-year correlation across consecutive seasons, both with a permutation null that shuffles opponent assignments. The trait claim is falsified if either reliability CI includes 0 or if the permutation null matches the observed value.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one primary reliability test. Apply Holm correction to the secondary metrics and halves. Report all tested metrics.
design.decision_rule: Gate: if split-half reliability of the adjusted defense effect across games is below 0.3 with a CI excluding 0 in the primary analysis, conclude 'no reliable team trait' and stop. Only if the gate passes, test year-to-year stability on the 90 consecutive-season pairs; a stable trait requires r at least 0.3 after adjustment, surviving the permutation null and Holm correction. Otherwise report uncertain or rejected.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for regular seasons 2022-23 to 2025-26 (2025-26 regular season complete as of 2026-04-13), with play-by-play, substitutions, starters, matchup minutes, and box scores. The 2025-26 playoffs are excluded before 2026-06-21. Pin the exact pull date and the derived play-type graph version.
